title: Iran and the New Rules of Global Power
gist: Robert Pape frames the 2026 Iran war as the bookend to an era that opened on 17 January 1991, when CNN's live broadcast of American precision-guided bombs hitting Baghdad command bunkers announced a new age of US military dominance over a seemingly formidable Iraq. The available text is only the opening section — the 'unmaking' half of the argument sits behind the paywall.

insights.claim: On the night of 17 January 1991, CNN broadcast the Gulf War live, showing American precision-guided bombs slamming into windows, air shafts and command bunkers in Baghdad — imagery that for millions signalled the arrival of a new age of warfare.
insights.speaker: Robert A. Pape
insights.so_what: Establishes the origin point of the precision-strike era whose end the article argues is now underway — the frame for judging today's munitions and airpower doctrine.
insights.quote: American precision-guided bombs slammed into windows, air shafts, and command bunkers in Baghdad

insights.claim: The 1991 images mattered because Iraq had looked genuinely threatening beforehand: Saddam Hussein commanded nearly one million armed men and an army that had survived eight years of brutal war with Iran.
insights.speaker: Robert A. Pape
insights.so_what: Baseline for judging perceived-versus-actual military capability — mass and combat experience were revealed as poor proxies for effectiveness against precision airpower.
insights.quote: Iraqi dictator Saddam Hussein commanded nearly one million armed men. His army had survived eight years of brutal war
insights.locator: To understand why those images mattered

themes.theme: Making and unmaking of American dominance

insights.claim: The article's stated frame is that the Iran war is rewriting the rules of global power and marks the unmaking of the American dominance that the 1991 Gulf War established.
insights.speaker: Robert A. Pape
insights.so_what: If US coercive airpower has lost its decisive edge, allied dependence on US security guarantees repricing becomes the dominant second-order trade.
insights.quote: Iran and the New Rules of Global PowerThe Making and Unmaking of American Dominance
insights.locator: Iran and the New Rules of Global Power

insights.claim: The argument comes from Robert A. Pape, University of Chicago political scientist, director of the Chicago Project on Security and Threats and author of 'Bombing to Win: Air Power and Coercion in War' — the leading sceptic on airpower's ability to coerce.
insights.speaker: Robert A. Pape
entities: Chicago Project on Security and Threats
insights.so_what: Source credibility matters here: the field's principal authority on the limits of strategic bombing is assessing the Iran campaign, so expect a negative verdict on coercion by air.
insights.locator: ROBERT A. PAPE is Professor of Political Science

insights.claim: The visual medium itself is treated as a driver of perceived power: live televised strike footage in 1991 shaped global beliefs about American capability for millions of viewers, independent of the underlying military balance.
insights.speaker: Robert A. Pape
insights.so_what: Perception of military dominance is media-mediated — relevant to how drone and missile footage from the 2026 conflicts is reshaping deterrence credibility.
insights.quote: For millions of people, the images seemed to herald the arrival of a new age.
insights.locator: CNN broadcast the Gulf War live

insights.claim: The captured text of this July 2026 analysis ends mid-sentence at the paywall after the 1991 Gulf War setup, so the specific evidence linking the Iran war to the erosion of US dominance is not available in this record.
insights.speaker: Robert A. Pape
